answer: Shared Journal Ledger. Each agent identity publishes a running hash-chained action log; every new agent must cite and get cosigned by two existing logs, which record the citation. A duplicate identity cannot cite its twin without creating a visible bridge between otherwise separate histories. Auditors flag these ripples of shared history as likely clones and quarantine both. An attacker must therefore maintain genuinely independent histories per clone or sacrifice a haven of unnoticed duplicates, costing weeks of logged work per identity.
